clue.text: (French) I desire to be chosen …

parts.note: je is the French word for I
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone confesses, half in French, a longing to be picked for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 4 across, which reuses this clue's desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jews are traditionally called the Chosen People in the Bible, so chosen serves as a fanciful stand-in for the adjective.

clue.text: 8 queen has to stick out about page 1

definitions.note: 8 down is DIVINE; read as a noun, a divine being, a god

indicators.note: about means going round, so the verb for sticking out surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: to jut is to stick out
P is the abbreviation for page
the Roman numeral for one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A cross-reference pretends a queen is forced to protrude around a numbered page.
explanation.walkthrough: JU(P I)T then ER. The queen comes first in the clue but last in the answer: she has the rest attached to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter was chief of the Roman gods, a divine being in the fullest sense of the cross-referenced word.

clue.text: O hark! the herald angels sing the Boy's descent which lifted up the world (anag), and in what circumstances

indicators.note: the setter simply labels the quoted carol line as letters to be rearranged

parts.words: O hark! the herald angels sing the Boy's descent which lifted up the world
parts.note: every letter of this carol line is used once

explanation.surface: Lines from one Christmas carol, with a question about when the singing happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder echoes Hark! the Herald Angels Sing; the answer is the opening of another carol, and it tells when the angels appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's opening line sets the scene of the Nativity announcement, answering the question of the circumstances in which the herald angels sang.

clue.text: See 2
… and (French) in this desire the requirement is no smoking

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the word for the desire, which wraps around them

parts.note: this desire points back to the wish of 1 across
F is the standard abbreviation for French
et is French for and, as the bracket says

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: the wish expressed is for a smoke-free room.
explanation.walkthrough: W(ET F)ISH. (French) does double duty: it marks and as French and supplies F. Wet fish is the British term for fresh, uncured fish sold by a fishmonger.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishmongers sell wet fish as opposed to kippers and other cured fish, so what this product needs is precisely not to have been smoked.

clue.text: See 2
See 2
I shall leave model X, not honestly come by

parts.note: I shall contracts to I'll
to go is to leave
the Model T was Ford's famous car
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.walkthrough: Model is not a fashion model but the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten describes property or gains acquired dishonestly, such as stolen money or loot.

clue.text: I enter with difficulty round the set, perhaps

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the single letter goes into the word for with difficulty

parts.note: as in breathing hard, with effort
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to get into a film or theatre set.
explanation.walkthrough: HA(I)RD then O. Set looks like a stage or film set, but a hairdresser's shampoo and set is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a hairstyle fixed in place while wet, one example of a styled arrangement of hair, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Dowse a theologian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to search for underground water with a rod
second meaning: a clergyman or scholar of religion

explanation.surface: An instruction to drench a religious scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Dowse is read as douse, to soak someone, but it is the water-finder's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Water diviners locate springs with a forked stick, and a learned churchman has long been called a divine.

clue.text: Catalogue of winners makes captured vessel lean over

parts.note: an enemy ship taken at sea is a prize
a ship lists when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: A ship seized in battle tilts to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll naming those awarded prizes, as published after a competition or school speech day.

clue.text: Alien form of Chou

definitions.note: the answer completes the name that begins with this word

indicators.note: a new form of something reshapes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign variant of a Chinese name.
explanation.walkthrough: Chou En-lai (now Zhou Enlai) was Premier of China under Mao.
explanation.definitionFit: These two syllables are the given name of the Chinese statesman whose surname appears in the clue.

clue.text: Effectiveness of choppers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: power to enforce, as a law with real bite
second meaning: slang for the things you chew with

explanation.surface: A question about how well axes or helicopters work.
explanation.walkthrough: Choppers suggests axes or helicopters; it is slang for what is in your mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule with no enforcement power is said to lack bite, and choppers is jokey slang for the mouth's biting equipment.

clue.text: In front of the forest I said I was a camera

definitions.note: names the one who said it: the writer

indicators.note: in front of places one piece directly before the other in the answer

parts.note: taken as written: the first I in the clue
the famous forest of Robin Hood, in Nottinghamshire

explanation.surface: A person standing before the trees recalls having claimed to be a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Isherwood's Goodbye to Berlin opens 'I am a camera', later a play title.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood, the novelist, wrote the line in his Berlin stories, describing his detached narrator recording everything.

clue.text: Spare man for game?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: held back for later, as a spare tank
second meaning: a substitute player in a team

explanation.walkthrough: Game also hints at a nature park for wild animals, a further sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute footballer sits on the bench in case needed, and a backup supply kept for emergencies is described the same way.

clue.text: Is Peter Simple a real person?

parts.note: the apostle Peter was first named Simon
pure and simple: unmixed, plain

explanation.surface: Asks whether Peter Simple, title character of Marryat's novel, actually existed.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Simple looks like one name, but splits into two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: In Centlivre's play A Bold Stroke for a Wife an impostor poses as Simon Pure, so the phrase came to mean the genuine article.

clue.text: Shortage is right in the end

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for right inside the word for the end

parts.note: death is the end of life
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that scarcity proves correct in the long run.
explanation.walkthrough: In the end reads as a phrase meaning eventually; here in is the container signal and the end is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something, as in a dearth of good candidates.

clue.text: See 2
First thought to be unlike Queen Victoria

parts.note: A is first, as in A1 or grade A
to muse is to ponder

explanation.surface: An initial impression that someone differed from the old Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously credited with the rebuke We are not amused.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria supposedly declared herself not entertained by a joke, so someone tickled by it is the opposite of her.

clue.text: Before the turn of Led Zeppelin's leader, time goes round in a confused state

indicators.note: goes round means the word for time surrounds the other letters
a turn moves the front letter of the band's first word round to the back
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the airship maker's initial
taken as written: the first word of the band name
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rock fan's tangled musing about the band's frontman and time passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Led Zeppelin's leader looks like Robert Plant, but the band name is split: the turn acts on the first word, the leader on the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Dazed means stunned and bewildered, so doing something dazedly is doing it while in a muddled state of mind.

clue.text: Precious writer has to tie wood backwards

indicators.note: backwards tells you to read the combined words from end to start

parts.note: to bind is to tie
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: An affected author is compelled to tie up timber the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Precious suggests a fussy author; the writer is a pen, and precious refers to its metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing tip of a quality fountain pen is often made of gold, a precious metal, and the pen point does the writing.

See 2
The Spanish Alonzo, leaderless, went round and round in Regent's Park

O is round in shape

explanation.definitionFit: The Zoological Society's famous zoo occupies the north side of Regent's Park, so the park is where it stands.

clue.text: See 2
The Spanish drink with marbles

definitions.note: the answer is the name that goes with Marbles

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A Spaniard has a drink while playing marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are classical Greek sculptures from the Parthenon, held in the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon sculptures to Britain, and they still bear his title as the Elgin Marbles.

clue.text: Appearance of a French dukedom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: outward form or semblance
second meaning: the ducal title of a powerful French family

explanation.surface: The look of a duke's French estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in disguise wears a false outward form, and the Dukes of Guise led the Catholic party in sixteenth-century France.

clue.text: Cox's first eater, not much to eat

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the apple variety is kept

parts.note: Cox is an apple variety
rust eats away at iron

explanation.surface: A Cox's Orange Pippin is a good eating apple, but a meagre meal.
explanation.walkthrough: An eater is also an eating apple, so the surface stays among fruit; here the eater is corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust of bread stands for a meagre ration, as in earning a crust or begging for a crust.

clue.text: Providing a hot dog, inn needs to take no action

indicators.note: providing food means preparing it, so the letters are made up into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub that serves hot dogs needs to sit back and do nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Providing reads as if, but works as making up the letters; the a is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from any action and staying idle is exactly the meaning of the verb phrase.

clue.text: Dramatic landscape?

parts.note: surface reading: spectacular natural countryside
setter's reading: belonging to drama, painted backdrops of a stage play

explanation.definitionFit: Theatre flats painted to look like countryside are the stage setting, and the word also means natural landscape.

clue.text: It requires a lot of exposure first to get old copper green

definitions.text: It requires a lot of exposure

parts.note: A is first, as in grade A
D was the abbreviation for the old penny, a copper coin
vert is green in heraldry and in French

explanation.surface: Turning old copper green takes a long time out in the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Exposure suggests weathering that turns copper to verdigris; here it means publicity. D stood for the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial or poster only works if many people see it, so publicity is its whole purpose.
